correctness.rationale: Because the carrier is finite, each neighbourhood family is finite. Repeated binary intersection puts its total intersection back in the family, and pairwise nonempty intersection applied at the last step makes that core nonempty. Since the core lies in every neighbourhood, existential subset tests and universal hitting tests are both exactly equivalent to their core versions, so structural induction preserves all formulas. Seriality and the converse singleton-family construction are immediate, and the tail example correctly separates the infinite case. The inspected verifier independently exhausts carriers through four worlds; the universal theorem rests on the finite-intersection proof.

originality.rationale: The primary source already supplies exactly the constructive forcing clauses and the three structural hypotheses: nonempty neighbourhood families for N, pairwise nonempty intersections for D, and binary-intersection closure for K. On a finite carrier, obtaining a least nonempty member by intersecting the finite family is an elementary consequence; once that member exists, both published modal clauses reduce to it by one-line subset/hitting equivalences. The serial relation and labelled count are then routine repackaging. Under the audit rule that corollaries and special cases are covered even without matching wording or counts, the claimed theorem is implication-level covered.

final_claim: On every finite constructive neighbourhood frame whose neighbourhood families are nonempty, binary-intersection closed, and pairwise intersecting, the total intersection at each world is a nonempty least neighbourhood; replacing each family by that singleton core preserves both constructive modal clauses and yields a serial relational presentation, with \((2^m-1)^m\) labelled cores on an \(m\)-world carrier.
limitations: This concerns the structural N/K/D frame conditions, not every frame that validates the corresponding formulas semantically.
The finite carrier is essential to the least-neighbourhood argument; the tail-family example only establishes failure of this principal reduction in general on infinite carriers.
